notes: Four chained security operations builds: (1) a rule engine that applies a JSON rule set to log files — counting matches and unique source IPs per rule and emitting alert.json/report.json with exact schemas, which must survive hidden rule/log sets including empty logs, missing rule keys, and regexes that raise re.error; (2) deterministic tar.gz snapshot sealed with gpg --symmetric --cipher-algo AES256 discovered from man gpg, with no plaintext archive left anywhere; (3) recovering an unknown 8-byte key from the cipher oracle via chosen zero-plaintext within a strict 25s wall-clock budget; (4) a pickle __reduce__ gadget whose load runs os.system and produces /app/pwn-proof.txt. reasoning_depth=3 from implementing the gpg option discovery (strongest of AES-128/192/256), the chosen-plaintext key fold, and robust defaulting for malformed rules; adversarial_inputs=2 from hidden edge/malformed rule+log sets and the oracle hidden re-key; hidden_case_generalization=3 because /app/detect.sh must run on brand-new rule/log sets and oracle.py must recover a fresh hidden key; resource_pressure=2 from the hard-time oracle budget.
